results.point_context:
### Where the rules draw the line

The legal picture is narrower than the technology picture. The Outer Space Treaty bans nuclear weapons and other weapons of mass destruction in orbit, as well as weapons on the Moon and other celestial bodies. It also requires space activity to follow international law. But it does not completely ban every conventional anti-satellite missile, jammer, or cyber operation. United Nations votes in 2024 and 2025 supported existing principles and further arms-control work, but they did not create a new comprehensive treaty. The U.S. pledge against destructive direct-ascent tests remains a national policy commitment.
